answer: When a pump station switches, a pressure wave travels through the water mains, so a claimant with a pressure sensor reports the wave's arrival time and the wave must match the utility's pump log. A raven flying over the district cannot carry the timing; a karst landscape of pipes gives each district its own travel time, and a cedar post beside the main feels the wave first, so three neighbours must agree, and a farm without sensors in that district cannot fabricate the arrival order.
